decisions.reason: The RR04 copy changes rely on its existing Lower Exposure classification but do not change the variant set, selection basis, or exposure-level mapping.
The footer correction is a separate amendment in the same message, not a consequence of the RR04 copy change; the required footer-code values were already established and remain unchanged.
The message reports that internal headers appear correct, while the RR04 wording amendments do not change any internal-header code requirement.
The message reports that main report codes appear correct; changing two RR04 narrative statements does not alter report-detail identifiers.
The RR04 narrative copy amendments do not change the dashboard fields, heading, prominence, visibility, or scope.
The revised RR04 wording does not change which customer fields must be editable or how the assessment-date field behaves.
The message's footer-code correction is independent of the RR04 copy modification, and the general footer style, information, and page coverage remain unchanged.
The RR04 copy amendments do not change internal-page header coverage, style, or information requirements.
The source changes two report statements for risk appropriateness but does not revise the established visual-design standard or design direction.
The 'What Matters Most' wording references security controls but does not change the requirement to present recommended actions clearly in prioritized tiers.
The source modifies RR04 section wording rather than the front-page explanation's content categories, bullet format, or concision requirement.
The RR04 narrative copy changes do not affect the scoring table's presentation, fields, or purpose.
